svg.aria-label: wf hello-ticket demo: a real run from entry to delivery
svg.title: wf: one ticket from entry to delivery (real output)

g.text: # The ticket, as a file in the repo
`greet('Ada')` returns `Hello, Ada!`. `greet()` with no name still returns `Hello!`.
# Admit it: wf opens an attempt with its own worktree and moves the ticket to In Progress
next: start the planner: `wf handoff planner --agent <id>`
tracker: admitted performed on the ticket files and read back
# The planner freezes the acceptance criteria before any code exists
Start agent type wf-planner (name it planner-1; do not pass a model) with: "Read ~/demo/hello-ticket/.wf-evidence/attempts/HT-1.1/handof
next: start the implementer: `wf handoff implementer --agent <id>` [wf-implementer]
# The implementer's first try forgets the comma
tracker: implementing performed on the ticket files and read back
Start agent type wf-implementer (name it implementer-1; do not pass a model) with: "Read ~/demo/hello-ticket/.wf-evidence/attempts/HT-1.
# No gate yet: the gate runs once a code-review round on this tree comes back clean
wf gate: the gate runs after a clean code review, never beside or before it:
- no review round covers the current tree: run the code review first (`wf handoff reviewer --agent <new id>`); the gate runs once a ro
und on this tree comes back clean
→ follow the order (`wf resume` names the next step), or run it anyway with `wf gate --reason "<why>"`, which records the override in
# The implementer cannot review its own work
wf handoff: implementer-1 planned, wrote or owns this change and cannot review it
# Code review, round 1: a fresh reviewer reads the diff against the criteria and finds the missing comma
Start agent type wf-reviewer (name it reviewer-1; do not pass a model) with only the line on stdout as its prompt:
# The implementer fixes the finding and commits
# Code review, round 2: a new reviewer judges the fixed tree blind, then verifies round 1's finding
Start agent type wf-reviewer (name it reviewer-2; do not pass a model) with only the line on stdout as its prompt:
1 finding(s) from earlier rounds to verify against the code: ~/demo/hello-ticket/.wf-worktrees/HT-1.1/_review/prior-findings-04-1.json
Add `priorFindings: [{ round, id, status, evidence }]` to your closure (change nothing else) and run `wf review --closure <file>` again.
# The review is clean: one gate on the reviewed tree
wf gate: run 2026-10-07T10-46-53-741Z-43765: 1 to run, 0 reused, 0 skipped or deferred
passed unit no `inputs` declared: always runs
# Evidence review: a fresh reviewer checks each criterion against the gate evidence
Start agent type wf-reviewer (name it reviewer-3; do not pass a model) with only the line on stdout as its prompt:
# Delivery: merged to main, pushed, and the ticket handed off
tracker: delivered performed on the ticket files and read back; attempt closed
SHOW TO OWNER: no screenshots for HT-1: no gate step declares `artifacts`, so the gate collected no screenshots
(recorded; tell the owner this in the delivery report)
next: nothing: this attempt is closed
# Readback: the ticket file as the engine left it, and main as pushed
`greet('Ada')` returns `Hello, Ada!`. `greet()` with no name still returns `Hello!`.
greet() now takes an optional name: greet("Ada") returns "Hello, Ada!".
next: nothing: this attempt is closed
